Class MoreElements

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.MoreElements
public final class MoreElements extends Object
Navigation, casts and checks on Elements that javax.lang.model does not provide.

The as... methods cast an element whose kind the caller knows, such as one annotated with an annotation that only targets types. They go by its kind, as Element recommends, and fail with a message naming the element and its kind, where a cast would throw a ClassCastException naming javac's implementation classes. To test an element whose kind is not known, check its kind instead.

    • isInnerClass

      public static boolean isInnerClass(Element element)
      Returns whether an element is an inner class: a nested class that is neither explicitly nor implicitly static, as JLS 8.1.3 defines it. An inner member class needs an instance of the class enclosing it to be created.

      A member class is inner unless it is declared static, or is a member of an interface or an annotation type, which makes it implicitly static. An enum, a record, an interface or an annotation type is never inner: it is implicitly static wherever it is nested.

      A local class is inner, and so is an anonymous class, the body of an enum constant included, as the language says: even in a static context, such as a static method or a static field initializer, where it has no enclosing instance. A local enum, record or interface is static.

      This goes by the static modifier, which Element.getModifiers() includes when it is implicit, for types read from class files too.

      Parameters:
      element - the element
      Returns:
      true if the element is an inner class; false if it is not a type

    • isStaticNested

      public static boolean isStaticNested(Element element)
      Returns whether an element is a nested class, interface, enum, record or annotation type that is static, explicitly or implicitly: a nested type that is not an inner class. A member type created without an instance of the class enclosing it is one, and so is a local enum, record or interface.
      Parameters:
      element - the element
      Returns:
      true if the element is a static nested type; false if it is not a type, or is top-level

    • visibility

      public static Visibility visibility(Element element)
      Returns the visibility an element is declared with: its access modifier, or the access the language gives it without one. It does not account for the types that enclose the element: effectiveVisibility(Element) does.

      Without an access modifier, a member of an interface or an annotation type is Visibility.PUBLIC, a constructor of an enum is Visibility.PRIVATE, and anything else is Visibility.PACKAGE. An enum constant is public, and so is a record component, which is read through its accessor, the private field that holds it being an element of its own. The constructor javac adds to a class that declares none, and the canonical constructor it adds to a record, have the visibility of their class, as the language says.

      An element that can only be named within a block or a declaration is Visibility.PRIVATE: a local or anonymous class, a type parameter, a parameter, a local variable, or an initializer. A package or a module is Visibility.PUBLIC: the language does not restrict access to them, and modules restrict access to their packages, as isExportedTo(Element, ModuleElement) checks.

      Parameters:
      element - the element
      Returns:
      its own visibility

    • effectiveVisibility

      public static Visibility effectiveVisibility(Element element)
      Returns the visibility an element has, given the types it is declared in: the most restrictive of its own visibility and that of each type, method or other element that encloses it, up to its package. A public method of a private nested class is private, and one of a package-private class is package-private. Anything declared in a local or anonymous class is private.

      This is the visibility of the element where it is declared. A member can be accessed through a subtype of the type that declares it, which may be more visible: a public method declared in a package-private class, and inherited by a public class, is package-private here, yet accessible from any package through that public class.

      Parameters:
      element - the element
      Returns:
      its effective visibility

    • isAccessible

      public static boolean isAccessible(Element element, String packageName)
      Returns whether code in a package can access an element, by the rules of JLS 6.6, from a class that does not extend the type that declares the element: generated code, unless it is such a subclass, which isAccessible(Element, String, TypeElement) checks.

      From the element's own package, anything but a private element is accessible, given its effective visibility. From another package, the element and every type that encloses it must be public: a protected member is not accessible. A private element is never accessible: the language allows it only within the top-level type that declares it, and generated code is in a top-level type of its own.

      This judges the element where it is declared, and leaves modules out. A member inherited by a more visible type, such as a public method of a package-private class inherited by a public class, is accessible through that type although this returns false for it: see effectiveVisibility(Element). Whether the element's module lets the code's module access it is isExportedTo(Element, ModuleElement).

      Parameters:
      element - the element to access, such as a type, a constructor, a method or a field
      packageName - the qualified name of the package of the code, empty for the unnamed package
      Returns:
      true if code in that package can access the element; true for a package or a module

    • isAccessible

      public static boolean isAccessible(Element element, String packageName, TypeElement superclass)
      Returns whether a class in a package that extends another class can access an element, as JLS 6.6 says: the generated subclass of a processor, for instance. Beyond what isAccessible(Element, String) allows, it can access from another package a protected member of its superclass, or of any class its superclass extends, provided the types that enclose that member are accessible too.

      Being accessible, a protected element can still only be used in some ways from another package, which this does not check (JLS 6.6.2). A protected instance field or method must be accessed through this, super, or an expression whose type is the subclass or one of its own subclasses, not through any instance of the superclass. A protected constructor can be invoked as super(...) from a constructor of the subclass, or to create an anonymous subclass, but not with new otherwise.

      Parameters:
      element - the element to access, such as a type, a constructor, a method or a field
      packageName - the qualified name of the package of the subclass, empty for the unnamed package
      superclass - the class the subclass extends, Object if it extends no other
      Returns:
      true if that subclass can access the element; true for a package or a module
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if superclass is an interface or an annotation type

    • isExportedTo

      public static boolean isExportedTo(Element element, ModuleElement module)
      Returns whether the module of an element lets code in another module access it: the code's module reads the element's module, and the element's module exports the element's package to it. Within a module, everything is exported.

      This goes by the module declarations, as JLS 7.7 says. A named module reads the modules it requires, and those they require transitively, java.base included; requires static counts, as it does at compile time. The unnamed module reads every module, but no named module reads it; it exports all its packages, as an automatic module does. What command-line options such as --add-reads and --add-exports change is not seen. Without modules, as when compiling for Java 8, everything is accessible.

      Generated code usually lands in the module of the elements it is generated for, which context.elements().getModuleOf(element) gives. The language rules within the module, such as access to a package-private type, are isAccessible(Element, String).

      Parameters:
      element - the element to access: a package, or an element in a package
      module - the module of the code that accesses it
      Returns:
      true if module can access the package of element
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the element is a module
